confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors are based on aggregated cost-of-living figures. MyLifeElsewhere lists an inexpensive meal at about $8.05, a domestic pint at about $2.42 and a cappuccino at about $2.36. TravelTables (last updated July 2023) lists a meal at about $7.30, beer at about $2.58, a cappuccino at about $1.67 and a mid-range meal for two at about $61.85. Those sources mostly reflect local, non-resort venues and part of the data is dated, so I raised the figures moderately for July 2026 and for the tourist-heavy Bávaro and Punta Cana restaurants visitors mostly use. My search found no aggregated cocktail or wine-by-the-glass prices, only venue-level per-person spend estimates. Cocktail and wine are therefore estimated from the local price relationship to beer and typical Caribbean tourist-bar pricing, so they are less certain. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge and not based on any booking-site or listing search. The registered hostel supply is thin and the market is dominated by all-inclusive resorts, so the hostel anchors are especially uncertain. July is shoulder or low season, which keeps the hotel estimates moderate.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink prices start from aggregated Punta Cana cost-of-living data and are adjusted upward for the resort-area tourist premium. Accommodation is benchmarked against other Caribbean beach-resort destinations such as Cancún and Playa del Carmen, adjusted for Punta Cana's weaker budget and hostel segment.
